outcome: No result found, in or out of the search window, that settles or moves whether GCH by itself implies the existence of an ℵ_2-Suslin tree; it remains open exactly as stated, and the live Wikipedia article on Suslin trees still calls it a longstanding open problem.
summary: The bullet asks a very specific question: does GCH alone (no extra combinatorial principle) force the existence of an ℵ_2-Suslin tree? This is distinct from, and easily conflated with, several nearby results that all involve additional hypotheses. Classical work (Jensen) shows GCH plus square at ℵ_1 gives an ℵ_2-Souslin tree, and it has long been known that if GCH holds and there are no ℵ_2-Souslin trees then ℵ_2 is weakly compact in L — but neither of these settles whether GCH alone suffices. The most relevant nearby paper, Neeman's 'The special Aronszajn tree property at ℵ_2 and GCH' (arXiv:1809.07638), was originally submitted 20 September 2018, well before the 26 January 2024 frozen revision; its April 2024 v7 revision (checked via WebFetch) is described as containing only corrections and improved explanations, not a new result, so it is not a within-window event, and in any case it builds a model of GCH + no ℵ_2-Souslin trees from a weakly compact cardinal — an independence/consistency result about the negation, not a proof that GCH implies existence, so it would not settle this bullet even if it were new. Other 2024-2026 papers surfaced by search (an almost-Kurepa Suslin tree paper arXiv:2406.10463, 'Two-cardinal Kurepa Hypotheses' arXiv:2510.08860, 'Full Souslin trees at small cardinals' arXiv:2308.00299, and 'Quagmires and large Suslin forests' arXiv:2608.28505, the last checked directly via WebFetch) all concern related but different objects — Kurepa trees, two-cardinal variants, full Souslin trees at small cardinals, and Suslin/Souslin forests at (ω_1,ω_2) — none of which is a case of or a resolution to 'GCH implies an ℵ_2-Suslin tree'. I also checked Assaf Rinot's blog, the most active researcher and blogger in this exact area, including his 'Open Problems' category, and found no post from 2024, 2025 or 2026 addressing this question; his most recent open-problems posts predate the window (November 2023 and earlier). No AI system appears anywhere in any source I opened. I agree with the triage verdict of 'none' and its reasoning.
competing_reading: One could argue the Neeman result (or the classical GCH+□(λ) result) is 'close enough' to count as touching this bullet's scope, since it fixes the sibling question (GCH + no ℵ_2-Souslin trees, consistency-wise) using large cardinals. But per §3.1, a related problem obtained by changing the question (asking about consistency of the negation given extra large-cardinal strength, rather than about what GCH alone entails) does not count as a case of this problem, and in any event the paper's substantive content predates the window.
what_would_settle_it: A proof either that GCH (with no further hypothesis) implies an ℵ_2-Suslin tree exists, or that GCH plus large cardinals/forcing axioms is consistent with there being no ℵ_2-Suslin tree without invoking anything beyond GCH itself, or a proof that the implication is independent of ZFC. Any of these appearing as a preprint or announcement after 26 January 2024 would change this record.
